title: UK GDP first quarterly estimate, Q4 2026 + December monthly GDP (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the Q4 outturn, published eight days after the February Monetary Policy Report
source: EST: two ONS release pages fetched direct 2026-09-10, HTTP 200 each — ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpfirstquarterlyestimateukoctobertodecember2026 reads verbatim 'GDP first quarterly estimate, UK: October to December 2026', 'Provisional release date: 12 February 2027', 'This release is not yet published'; ons.gov.uk/releases/gdpmonthlyestimateukdecember2026 reads 'Release date: 12 February 2027 7:00am' for the December monthly bulletin, so both ship the same morning. NOTE THE PUBLISHER'S OWN DISTINCTION: the quarterly page carries a 'Provisional release date' while every monthly page in this family carries a plain 'Release date' — the ONS treats the quarterly slot as provisional and the monthly slot as firm, and this entry inherits the weaker of the two. Filed estimate on three counts: that provisional label, the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts having no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics, and this lane's no-self-confirm limit
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-gdp-monthly-2027-01-15 LANE, 2026-09-10, during that event's never-assessed initial research. Proposed because it is the load-bearing date under that lane's central finding and the finding is measurably weaker without it on the calendar. TWO REASONS IT EARNS A SLOT. FIRST, IT IS THE EIGHT-DAY GAP ITSELF: the Bank of England's upcoming-MPC-dates page (fetched direct 2026-09-10) lists 'Thursday 4 February' 2027 under '2027 provisional dates' as the February MPC Summary AND Monetary Policy Report. This release is EIGHT DAYS LATER, which is what makes 'the February 2027 MPR's Q4 GDP figure is a nowcast, not an outturn' a dated claim rather than a rhetorical one — at the moment that Report publishes, no ONS Q4 2026 outturn exists. SECOND, IT IS THE ADJUDICATING VENUE: the proposing ledger measures that a two-month partial (October + November, flat December carry) explains R2 = +0.810 of Q4 q/q variance with MAE 0.124pp across eleven post-2013 ex-COVID Q4s, against R2 = +0.549 / MAE 0.161pp knowing October alone. This print is the outturn that scores that arithmetic. It also pairs the quarter's first estimate with the third month's monthly bulletin, which is the ONS's standing habit — the Q3 2026 equivalent (gdpfirstquarterlyestimateukjulytoseptember2026, fetched the same day) reads 'Release date: 12 November 2026 7:00am', the same morning as the September monthly print. The proposing lane makes NO claim about this release's market impact: symbols is empty, no instrument script was run, and the LOW tier is inherited from the ONS family and from the absence of any transmission path — the ten tracked names are all US-listed and no house playbook carries a gilt or sterling leg. ID PREFIX NOTE: uk-gdp-* is used for consistency with the canonical uk-gdp-monthly-2027-01-15.json written by the same lane on the same day; a sibling lane has a competing proposal under the opposite uk-monthly-gdp-* prefix (proposals/uk-monthly-gdp-2026-10-15.from-uk-blue-book-2026-10-30.json), flagged there and here, and not this lane's to rename. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
